required_presentation_changes.prior: DOE's Thacker Pass record fixes a federal loan of approximately $2.26 billion and describes facilities designed for about 40,000 tonnes of battery-grade lithium carbonate annually. It identifies a financing commitment and a proposed product, giving the project more specificity than a general statement about lithium demand. The designed output remains a target in this evidence account.
required_presentation_changes.replacement: The retained DOE account records an October 2024 loan closing of approximately $2.26 billion, comprising principal and capitalized interest, for facilities designed to produce about 40,000 tonnes of battery-grade lithium carbonate annually. That is a dated financing milestone and a proposed product/output specification, not a new commitment discovered in this assessment. The design target is not observed annual production, and the loan's face value is not proof of drawdown or accepted construction.

required_presentation_changes.prior: The paired Nevada case also includes Rhyolite Ridge's water-pollution-control permit. Its pre-operation structure includes notice, inspection, modeling, monitoring, reporting and closure conditions. These requirements give investigators a practical sequence of records to seek. They also show why a permit title is not an adequate summary of the project's operating position.
required_presentation_changes.replacement: The Nevada case also includes Rhyolite Ridge's water-pollution-control permit. Its retained profile distinguishes pre-operation notice and inspection from modeling, monitoring, reporting and closure requirements that apply at their specified stages. These conditions provide records to seek; they should not all be relabelled pre-operation tasks or treated as satisfied because a permit exists. This assessment does not newly inspect the permit, later amendments or current compliance.

required_presentation_changes.prior: Reclamation's framework supplies expected reservoir conditions and an initially expected water-year 2027 release of 6.0–7.0 million acre-feet, subject to adjustment through April. ADWR's Phoenix Version 3 memorandum models unmet demand over a 100-year horizon. These are not two measurements of the same outcome: one concerns reservoir operations and the other a regional groundwater model with its own assumptions and observational basis.
required_presentation_changes.replacement: The retained Reclamation account gives an initially expected water-year 2027 release of 6.0–7.0 million acre-feet, subject to adjustment through April; the earlier September 22 HTML check supplies that exact adjustment locator. ADWR's Phoenix Version 3 memorandum uses observed inputs through 2023 and a modeled 2024–2123 horizon. These are not two observed measures of one outcome: reservoir operating expectations and a regional groundwater model have different scopes, assumptions and decision roles. No underlying model reconstruction, later revision check or facility water-balance verification was performed here.

required_presentation_changes.prior: A facility water claim would require a further link to the responsible provider, applicable permissions and actual service. The TSMC wastewater agreement supplies one project-specific instrument, but it still does not establish completed, accepted water infrastructure. This is the same documentary discipline used in procurement: locate the applicable authority, then verify the named implementation and receiving party.
required_presentation_changes.replacement: A facility water claim needs a link to the responsible provider, applicable instruments and actual service. For TSMC, the retained September 22 check located Phoenix Council adoption of the wastewater authorization and conditional infrastructure terms. That does not establish an executed agreement, completed work, accepted assets or an operating reclaimed-water plant. No qualifying measured facility return was retrieved in that bounded check; nonexistence is not inferred. The procurement analogy remains a method: identify the authority, then verify the named implementation and receiver.

required_presentation_changes.replacement: The retained June 2026 ADA report describes eleven station projects reaching substantial completion and eight reaching final completion between November 1, 2025 and April 30, 2026. These are separate named lists, not nineteen unique completed stations. Substantial completion means primary-scope completion and turnover for passenger use, with possible residual work; it is not final completion or measured feature uptime. This assessment reuses the retained cohort records and does not newly inspect the PDF or observe passenger use.

required_presentation_changes.prior: The same report separates PIDS deployment from final FRA closeout. An installed passenger-information system can therefore have a different administrative state from a station construction project. required_presentation_changes.replacement: PIDS deployment is a different scope from station construction and final FRA closeout. A pending target date is not an acceptance event, and the bounded failure to retrieve a qualifying closeout is not proof that none exists. Neither inventory measures display uptime, trip usability or passengers' experience over repeated journeys.
